newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close sharply mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close sharply mixed.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed very mixed as September held strength on demand for deliverable supplies and November crashed late on a combination of fund selling and seasonal pressure, traders said.

Futures started very weak with November opening down the $10.00 per tbf limit before prices rallied following the developing strength in September. September was considered a very good buy as it equals $406 cost after deduction for shipping costs while cash is $432 per tbf, traders said.
But back months again turned down late paced by November which was considered very overbought.

Late selling by Cargill Investor Services touched off sell stops in November. That month, despite being at a sharp disount to the September level, represents the weakest period seasonally for lumber, they said.

"Traders that are looking a little longer term are looking for a seasonal slowdown in the housing market and were more apt to sell the November and January" said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Lumber closed up $5.90 in September at $413.90 and off $9.00 in November at $365.50 per tbf.
